qs.q: A pathology report describes atypical lobular hyperplasia in a breast biopsy specimen. Which histological criterion distinguishes atypical lobular hyperplasia from lobular carcinoma in situ?
o: Cells filling less than 50% of the acini within a single lobule
Presence of prominent branching fibrovascular cores within the acini
Dyscohesive cells with loss of E-cadherin expression
Complete architectural effacement of the entire terminal duct lobular unit
qs.e: Atypical lobular hyperplasia and lobular carcinoma in situ share identical dyscohesive cells with loss of E-cadherin, but ALH cells fill less than 50% of the acini in a lobule while LCIS fills more than 50%. Both lesions represent proliferative disease with atypia.
